See also: Lupo

Aragonese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • llop (Ribagorzan)

Etymology

[edit]

From Vulgar Latin *lūpum, from Latin lŭpum.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlupo/
  • Syllabification: lu‧po
  • Rhymes: -upo

Noun

[edit]

lupo m (plural lupos)

  1. wolf

References

[edit]
  • “lobo”, in Aragonario, diccionario castellano–aragonés (in Spanish)

Cebuano

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Hyphenation: lu‧po

Etymology 1

[edit]

Ultimately inherited from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *nəpuq, with an irregular initial lateral.

Noun

[edit]

lupo

  1. the black smooth stingfish (Tetraroge niger)

Etymology 2

[edit]

By metathesis. From luop.

Verb

[edit]

lupo

  1. to block off

Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
lupo
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin lupus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlupo/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Audio 3:(file)
  • Rhymes: -upo
  • Syllabification: lu‧po

Noun

[edit]

lupo (accusative singular lupon, plural lupoj, accusative plural lupojn)

  1. wolf

Hypernyms

[edit]
  • kanisedo (“canid”)

Hyponyms

[edit]
  • lupidino (“female wolf cub”)
  • lupido (“wolf cub”)
  • lupino (“she-wolf”)
  • virlupo (“male wolf”)

Holonyms

[edit]
  • luparo (“pack of wolves”)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • lupa (“lupine”)
  • lupfantomo (“werewolf”)
  • lupfaŭko (“snapdragon”)
  • lupfiŝo (“wolffish”)

Related terms

[edit]
  • lupolo

Further reading

[edit]
  • “lupo”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “lupo”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-present

Anagrams

[edit]
  • pulo

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from English loupe, French loupe, German Lupe and Spanish lupa. (Compare Esperanto lupeo).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlupɔ/

Noun

[edit]

lupo (plural lupi)

  1. (simple) magnifying glass, reading glass, pocket lens

See also

[edit]
  • lenso
  • mikroskopo

Italian

[edit]
Italian Wikipedia has an article on:
lupo
Wikipedia it

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • lopo (regional, Romanesco, archaic, directly from Latin lŭpum)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *lūpum, from Latin lŭpum. Doublet of lupus and lovo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlu.po/
  • Audio (un lupo):(file)
  • Rhymes: -upo
  • Hyphenation: lù‧po

Noun

[edit]

lupo m (plural lupi, feminine lupa)

  1. wolf

Hypernyms

[edit]
  • canide

Derived terms

[edit]
  • allupare
  • cane lupo
  • fame da lupo
  • il lupo perde il pelo ma non il vizio
  • in bocca al lupo
  • lupacchiotto
  • lupara
  • lupesco
  • lupetto
  • lupino
  • lupo di mare
  • tempo da lupi

Related terms

[edit]
  • lupanare
  • luppolo
  • lupus

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Sardinian: lupu

Anagrams

[edit]
  • -uplo, pulo

Latin

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

lupō

  1. dative/ablative singular of lupus

Neapolitan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin lupus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Naples) IPA(key): [ˈluːpə]
  • (Castelmezzano) IPA(key): [ˈluːpə]

Noun

[edit]

lupo m (plural lupe, feminine singular lopa, feminine plural lope)

  1. wolf (male)

References

[edit]
  • AIS: Sprach- und Sachatlas Italiens und der Südschweiz [Linguistic and Ethnographic Atlas of Italy and Southern Switzerland] – map 434: “il lupo” – on navigais-web.pd.istc.cnr.it

Polish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlu.pɔ/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -upɔ
  • Syllabification: lu‧po

Noun

[edit]

lupo f

  1. vocative singular of lupa

Serbo-Croatian

Noun

lupo (Cyrillic spelling лупо)

  1. vocative singular of lupa

Swedish

[edit]

lupo
